ruling.note: Owner's ruling (2026-11-12): 241219BRY is pooled 3' prime-seq (owner's ruling 2026-10-27, see expression-two-groups). 3' reads do not cover the HLA class I exons, so refusing to build hlatyping is correct. The 2026-10-26 migrated ruling, which expected an hlatyping build, predates the pool ruling. The story now expects a reasoned refusal and no launch.

stories.question: Which HLA alleles does this donor carry?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: 241219BRY is pooled 3' prime-seq (SOP 65): barcoded oligo(dT) libraries read from the 3' end, one read only barcode and UMI. These reads do not cover the HLA class I exons, so hlatyping cannot resolve the donor's alleles from them. The right reply refuses with that reason, may say which reads would work (WES, WGS or full-length RNA-seq), and builds nothing.

ruling.note: Ruled by an independent Fable reviewer agent on the owner's instruction (2026-10-26).

stories.question: Which HLA class I alleles does each donor have, from their whole-genome sequencing?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Migrated from the old DNA selection cases; answers unchanged.

ruling.note: Ruled by an independent reviewer sub-agent on the owner's instruction (2026-11-13). As proposed, it repeated dna-hla-from-wgs almost word for word in meaning: same cohort, same acceptable, must_not and launch, with 'HLA-A, -B and -C types' for 'class I alleles'. It added little beyond keeping hlatyping at the four-story floor (test_every_choosable_pipeline_has_at_least_four_stories), and it is needed for that. The answer stays hlatyping, built, with sarek and rnavar as must_not; that is right for the human PCR-free WGS cohort, since OptiType types class I from genomic reads. The question becomes an outcome phrasing that asks for the deliverable qout-allele-calls asks for (two-field calls of the A*02:01 kind). The pair now tests one request with opposite verdicts: refused on pooled 3' prime-seq, built on WGS.

stories.question: I need two-field HLA-A, -B and -C allele calls, the A*02:01 kind, for each donor in these genome samples.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Human whole-genome germline DNA: two PBMC donors, Illumina DNA PCR-Free libraries, LibraryStrategy WGS, LibrarySource GENOMIC, paired 2x150. Genomic reads cover the HLA class I exons, so hlatyping (OptiType, seq_type dna) returns two-field HLA-A, -B and -C calls per donor, the deliverable named. This is the counterpart of qout-allele-calls, where the same request on pooled 3' prime-seq is refused. sarek reports variants genome-wide and does not type HLA (atlas sarek-vs-hlatyping); rnavar needs RNA.

ruling.note: Ruled by an independent reviewer sub-agent on the owner's instruction (2026-11-13). test::human_exome is two human lymphoblastoid lines, Agilent SureSelect Human All Exon V7 hybrid capture, LibraryStrategy WXS / Targeted Capture, GENOMIC. The hlatyping atlas entry lists WXS and targeted capture, and the capture covers the class I exons, so hlatyping (seq_type dna) built is right. sarek (does not type HLA) and rnavar (RNA only) are correctly must_not. No existing story covers HLA typing from exome.

stories.question: Can you get each donor's HLA class I genotype from my exome samples?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Human whole-exome with a named capture kit (Agilent SureSelect Human All Exon V7): the capture covers the HLA class I exons, so hlatyping (seq_type dna) calls the alleles. sarek calls variants, not HLA alleles; rnavar needs RNA.

ruling.note: Ruled by an independent reviewer sub-agent on the owner's instruction (2026-11-13). 240709KAM is human (CEL Species Homo sapiens) MDA-MB-231, total RNA with NEBNext Ultra II Directional, paired-end 2x50, LibrarySource Transcriptomic, raw reads on SRA. This is a whole-transcript library, not a 3' or pooled prep, so hlatyping (seq_type rna) can type the expressed class I alleles. hlatyping passes its human-only constraint, and a build is right. rnaseq, rnavar and rnafusion none type HLA (atlas versus entries). It is a useful positive contrast to the three 241219BRY refusals.

stories.question: Which HLA class I alleles does this breast cancer line carry, going by my RNA-seq samples?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Human bulk paired-end full-length RNA-seq of MDA-MB-231 cells, with raw reads on SRA: the expressed HLA class I transcripts are covered end to end, so hlatyping (seq_type rna) calls the alleles. Contrast with the 241219BRY HLA stories, whose pooled 3' prime-seq reads do not cover those exons. rnaseq counts genes, rnavar calls variants and rnafusion calls fusions; none types HLA.
